A.text: Each patient's needs determine which systemic and topical products, in the clinic or at home, are appropriate.

B.text: Product selection is driven by the individual patient's needs, so a single product for everyone is not guidance.

C.text: Supplement recommendations also depend on water fluoride level, other dietary fluoride, toothpaste use, and caries risk, so age alone is not sufficient.

D.text: Appropriate amounts of over-the-counter fluoride toothpaste are the first line for caries prevention, so toothpaste is not delayed until professional agents are applied.

E.text: For patients with special health care needs, brushing twice daily with fluoridated dentifrice helps prevent caries and gingivitis, so it should not be avoided.

explanation.text: Fluoride product choice, systemic or topical and in-office or at-home, is individualized to the patient's specific needs.
Supplement decisions weigh several factors, not age alone.
Fluoridated toothpaste is first line and is recommended for patients with special health care needs.
